name: Marcus T.
text: This is spot on. I went to a dinner last month where they piped in this subtle lavender and they literally recreated the entire experience using just scent cues. My wife couldn't stop talking about how it made her feel transported.

name: Jennifer K.
text: Great article but I'm curious about the cost of implementing custom scent design. Does anyone know if this is only for ultra-luxury events or can mid-range restaurants do this too?

name: David R.
text: Honestly felt a bit gimmicky when I first heard about scent marketing, but after attending one of these events I completely get it now. The food tasted better somehow.

name: Sophia L.
text: I work in event planning and we've been hesitant about scent design because of allergies. Would love to see more discussion about how to do this responsibly without excluding guests.

name: Thomas M.
text: The olfactory memory thing is real. Went to a dinner 5 years ago that used rose and cedarwood, and I still remember it vividly when I smell those notes. Nothing else from that night sticks with me like the scent does.
